  • GetServiceAccount (/storage/v1/projects/{project}/serviceAccount), the principal Cloud Storage publishes as; grant it publish rights before wiring notifications
  • hmacKeys create/list/get/update/delete (/storage/v1/projects/{project}/hmacKeys), the credentials S3-compatible clients present to GCS; the secret is returned once on create, and a key must be INACTIVE before it can be deleted

Object operations (REST XML + REST JSON):

  • PutObject (simple and multipart/resumable upload)
  • GetObject
  • DeleteObject
  • ListObjects (with pageToken, prefix, delimiter pagination, plus startOffset, endOffset, matchGlob and includeTrailingDelimiter filtering)
  • Decompressive transcoding (an object stored with contentEncoding: gzip is served decompressed to a client that did not send Accept-Encoding: gzip, and as stored to one that did; Range is ignored on a transcoded read)
  • CopyObject
  • MoveObject
  • HeadObject
  • PatchObject (update metadata: contentType, contentDisposition, contentEncoding, contentLanguage, cacheControl, customTime, custom metadata)
  • System metadata at upload time (contentEncoding, contentDisposition, contentLanguage, cacheControl, customTime, storageClass) in the JSON metadata part of a multipart/resumable upload; on the upload URL only contentEncoding is honoured, as on GCS
  • customTime follows the GCS rules: rendered in UTC, never removed once set (a null patch or an unset gRPC custom_time under the mask is a no-op), and a decrease is rejected with 400 / INVALID_ARGUMENT
  • ComposeObject (concatenate 1 to 32 source objects; 0 or more than 32 is a 400)
  • RewriteObject (multi-call when the source and destination span storage classes or bucket locations: a maxBytesRewrittenPerCall, which must be a multiple of 1 MiB, below the object size returns done: false with a rewriteToken and the client loops until it completes; a same-class, same-location copy finishes in one call whatever limit is sent, as in GCS)
  • hmacKeys are stored through the emulator's storage backend, so they survive restarts in persistent mode and are cleared by the reset endpoint
  • Soft delete (softDeletePolicy on the bucket, ?softDeleted=true listing, objects.restore). A bucket created without a policy gets the GCS default of retentionDurationSeconds: "604800" (7 days), REST and gRPC alike. 0 turns soft delete off, and any other value must fall between 7 and 90 days, otherwise the request fails with 400 and reason: invalid. Without Object Versioning, an object replaced by an upload, compose, copy, rewrite or move is soft-deleted, as a deleted one is; with versioning it becomes noncurrent. effectiveTime is set by the server and moves forward when the retention grows. Buckets saved by older emulator versions keep the policy they had. Once its hardDeleteTime passes, a soft-deleted object leaves the listing and can no longer be restored, and a background sweep frees its bytes
  • Pre-signed GET/PUT URLs (V4 signature via IAM SignBlob)
  • Batch requests (/batch/storage/v1), including when the container's published port differs from its internal one (docker run -p 9000:4588)
  • Customer-supplied encryption keys (CSEK)

Object names containing /, spaces, +, or percent-encoded sequences round-trip correctly, the emulator preserves URI-encoded names exactly as real GCS does.

Pub/Sub notifications (REST JSON):

  • CreateNotification / ListNotifications / GetNotification / DeleteNotification (/storage/v1/b/{bucket}/notificationConfigs), object changes publish to the configured Pub/Sub topic in the local backend

Object ACLs (REST JSON):

  • ListObjectAcl / CreateObjectAcl

  • GetObjectAcl / UpdateObjectAcl / DeleteObjectAcl

docs.title: IAM allow-policy enforcement
docs.text:
Set FLOCI_GCP_SERVICES_IAM_AUTHORIZATION_MODE=enforce to evaluate supported bucket IAM allow policies for REST JSON and XML bucket and object operations. GCS gRPC v2 remains outside IAM allow-policy enforcement; its existing Credential Access Boundary checks still apply. The default remains disabled, preserving the emulator's no-auth behavior. See the IAM service for supported principals, roles, conditions, bootstrap administration, and intentional exclusions.

Conditional requests (preconditions):

  • ifGenerationMatch / ifGenerationNotMatch
  • ifMetagenerationMatch / ifMetagenerationNotMatch
  • ifSourceGenerationMatch / ifSourceGenerationNotMatch for object moves
  • ifSourceMetagenerationMatch / ifSourceMetagenerationNotMatch for object moves
  • Returns HTTP 412 on precondition failure
  • Enforced atomically on object mutation paths under object locks, with a monotonic generation sequence, concurrent writers with ifGenerationMatch=0 race safely (exactly one wins)

docs.title: XML multipart uploads
docs.text:
Native XML object routes support POST ?uploads, PUT ?uploadId=...&partNumber=..., GET parts, POST completion and DELETE abort. Bucket GET ?uploads lists pending uploads with prefix and key/upload-ID markers. Parts and sessions use StorageFactory and survive graceful restarts in persistent, hybrid and WAL modes. Incomplete uploads do not appear in ordinary object inventory.

Part numbers range from 1 to 10000. Completion validates increasing order, ETags and the 5 MiB minimum for every non-final part. Retrying a part replaces that part; a failed completion preserves the session. A part receipt in the completion is accepted with or without its quotes. A receipt that names a part that was not uploaded, or a wrong ETag, returns HTTP 404 NoSuchPart. The completion result is sent the way GCS sends it: as text/html, with the ETag in the body only, a Location that is the XML URL of the object, and the x-goog-stored-content-length, x-goog-hash, x-goog-generation and x-goog-metageneration headers. Completed objects have CRC32C and the multipart ETag described under XML API entity tags, but no MD5 hash. Multipart upload delimiter grouping, customer-supplied encryption, upload preconditions and lifecycle expiry of incomplete sessions are unsupported. The emulator buffers parts and completed bytes in memory. Object publication and session removal are separate checkpoints; crash-atomic completion across those stores is not guaranteed.

Authentication retains the existing emulator credential acceptance and CAB checks. In IAM enforce mode, every XML multipart request also evaluates its documented storage.multipartUploads.* and object permissions; an upload ID is not an authenticator. Signed URL expiry checks do not prove cryptographic signature enforcement. The SDK suite uses only synthetic credentials and fixture signing keys.

Multipart object metadata is finalized before storage publication and Pub/Sub or Eventarc finalization events. The event and stored generation agree on the ETag, CRC32C, content metadata and absence of MD5. Ordinary uploads continue to include their MD5. Object publication and multipart-session removal still use separate checkpoints; crash-atomic multipart completion is not guaranteed.

docs.title: XML API entity tags
docs.text: The XML API writes the ETag header of PUT, GET and HEAD, the ETag element of ListObjects and the result of a multipart completion the way GCS does, in quotes. An object with an MD5 carries that MD5 in hex. A multipart upload carries the MD5 of its part digests, a dash and the part count. A composite object, which has no MD5, carries a dash followed by its resource etag. The JSON API, including alt=media downloads, keeps the resource etag of the object.

docs.title: XML API object listing
docs.text:
GET /{bucket} answers with ListBucketResult the way GCS does. Without list-type, or with any value other than 2, the result has the version 1 shape: Name, Prefix, Marker, NextMarker when the page is truncated, MaxKeys when max-keys was sent, Delimiter when delimiter was sent, IsTruncated, then every Contents entry and then every CommonPrefixes entry. list-type=2 replaces Marker and NextMarker with StartAfter, ContinuationToken and NextContinuationToken, and adds KeyCount, the number of Contents entries on the page. A continuation-token wins over start-after. A marker sent with list-type=2 returns HTTP 400 NotImplemented. A token the emulator did not issue returns HTTP 400 InvalidArgument.

A page holds at most max-keys entries, objects and common prefixes together, in name order. max-keys=0 returns an empty page that is not truncated. A negative max-keys is ignored, and a value that is not a number returns HTTP 400 InvalidArgument. Without max-keys the emulator returns every entry on one page.

Each Contents entry carries Key, Generation, MetaGeneration, LastModified, ETag and Size. encoding-type=url URL-encodes Prefix, Marker, NextMarker, StartAfter, Delimiter, every Key and every common prefix the way GCS does: a space becomes +, the characters ! $ ' ( ) * , ; : @ / ? stay as they are, and everything else outside letters, digits, -, ., _ and ~ becomes a percent escape. The result then carries Encoding-Type in version 1 and EncodingType in version 2. The response carries the bucket metageneration in x-goog-metageneration. The versions listing is not supported over XML.

docs.title: XML API error responses
docs.text:
Failures from supported XML object transfers, listings, and multipart operations use application/xml with an Error root, a machine-readable Code, and a Message. This does not depend on the request's Accept header. Missing buckets, objects (including generations), and multipart uploads return distinct NoSuchBucket, NoSuchKey, and NoSuchUpload codes with HTTP 404. A completion that names an unknown part or a wrong part ETag returns NoSuchPart with HTTP 404. Other multipart receipt and checksum errors retain their specific codes. Signed URL errors retain their optional Details and ParameterName fields.

Anonymous permission denial returns HTTP 403 AccessDenied. A denied request whose credentials resolve as external or unsupported returns HTTP 401 AuthenticationRequired. Unknown Floci tokens also return AuthenticationRequired; expired Floci tokens return InvalidAuthentication on every retry. HTTP 401 XML responses include a WWW-Authenticate: Bearer challenge. These failures use a fixed message and a separate Details element for the failure explanation. Valid credentials rejected by IAM or their Credential Access Boundary return HTTP 403 AccessDenied.

The emulator still accepts external credentials when an operation is allowed by its configured authorization mode and policies. This remains an intentional emulator behavior, rather than cryptographic validation of external credentials. Expired Floci credential records are retained until credential state is cleared, so repeated lookups can distinguish expiry from an unknown token; they never authorize a request.

Unexpected storage and backend failures return a sanitized HTTP 500 InternalError. Their diagnostic exceptions are logged on the server. GCS JSON and gRPC errors keep their existing contracts.

This mapping covers failures raised while executing the selected XML resource. Pre-resource routing, filters that abort a request, and response serialization failures remain separate framework boundaries. Service Usage retains its existing XML denial response. Exact messages for all upstream failures have not been validated against live GCS; the status and code mappings follow the Cloud Storage XML status reference, and credential distinctions follow the live observations recorded in issue #282.

docs.title: GKE (Kubernetes Engine)
docs.text: floci-gcp emulates the Google Kubernetes Engine control plane (container.googleapis.com, ClusterManager v1) over REST JSON. Cluster lifecycle is backed by real k3s containers (rancher/k3s) started through the host Docker daemon, or a lightweight mock mode.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Variable Default Description FLOCI_GCP_SERVICES_GKE_ENABLED true Enable/disable GKE FLOCI_GCP_SERVICES_GKE_MOCK false Mock mode: clusters return RUNNING immediately without starting a k3s container FLOCI_GCP_SERVICES_GKE_DEFAULT_IMAGE rancher/k3s:latest Image used for real clusters FLOCI_GCP_SERVICES_GKE_API_SERVER_BASE_PORT 6550 Start of the host port range for k3s API servers FLOCI_GCP_SERVICES_GKE_API_SERVER_MAX_PORT 6599 End of the host port range FLOCI_GCP_SERVICES_GKE_ENDPOINT_MODE host How the cluster endpoint is advertised to kubectl (host for a reachable host:port) FLOCI_GCP_SERVICES_GKE_KEEP_RUNNING_ON_SHUTDOWN false Leave spawned k3s containers running after floci-gcp shuts down FLOCI_GCP_SERVICES_GKE_DOCKER_NETWORK (none) Overrides FLOCI_GCP_SERVICES_DOCKER_NETWORK for GKE/k3s sidecars only

docs.title: Routing: how clients reach GKE
docs.text:
On real GCP, container.googleapis.com and other APIs share the canonical /v1/projects/.../clusters path and are told apart only by hostname. floci-gcp serves everything on one port, where that path also belongs to Managed Kafka, so GKE mounts under a /container prefix and a routing filter maps clients onto it two ways:

  • Host mode (SDKs, Terraform/OpenTofu): point the client endpoint host at container.* (e.g. http://container.localhost:4588). The first DNS label container triggers a rewrite of /v1/... to /container/v1/.... container.localhost resolves to loopback out of the box on most systems (systemd-resolved's synthetic *.localhost wildcard on Linux; no /etc/hosts edit needed on macOS either).
  • Path mode (gcloud / direct): call the /container/v1/... prefix directly, or set a custom endpoint base of <endpoint>/container/v1/.

docs.title: API versions
docs.text:
GKE is served under both v1 and v1beta1, which declare the same HTTP bindings, so either mode above works with either version (/v1beta1/... on a container.* host, or /container/v1beta1/...). The google-beta Terraform provider and Pulumi gcp (bridged from it) always call v1beta1; point them at the same host mode endpoint (container_custom_endpoint = "http://container.localhost:4588/").

  • Both versions share the same handlers and the same store: a cluster created on one is visible on the other.
  • Fields that only v1beta1 defines (for example workloadAltsConfig, protectConfig, nodeConfig.hostMaintenancePolicy) are accepted and ignored, like any field the emulator does not model. Set to a non-default value, they are named in a DEBUG log line.
  • selfLink always uses /container/v1/.
  • The v1beta1-only ListLocations method returns 501 UNIMPLEMENTED.
  • Any other API version (/v2/... on a container.* host, or /container/v2/...) returns a JSON 404 NOT_FOUND naming the path.

Terraform/OpenTofu must use host mode, not path mode

The hashicorp/google provider's GKE client resolves its base URL through a RemoveBasePathVersion helper that strips the last path segment of any custom endpoint, on the assumption it is a stray API version suffix (.../v1/). Given a path-prefixed endpoint like <endpoint>/container/, it incorrectly strips container too, so container_custom_endpoint = "<endpoint>/container/" silently resolves to bare <endpoint>/ and every GKE call 404s or is routed to whatever other service happens to own that raw /v1/projects/.../locations/.../clusters path (Managed Kafka, in this codebase). Set container_custom_endpoint = "http://container.localhost:4588/" (host mode) instead. Not yet wired into compatibility-tests/compat-terraform's CI suite — that suite's floci-gcp container is reached as floci-gcp:4588 on the shared Docker network, so a container.* host override needs a network alias (or /etc/hosts entry) for container.floci-gcp in compatibility.yml, not just the *.localhost wildcard resolution local dev gets for free. Verified manually against ./mvnw quarkus:dev instead; see the PR description for the exact commands.

SDK transport

The Cloud Client libraries default to gRPC, which the REST-only emulator does not serve for GKE. Build the client with the HttpJson transport (ClusterManagerSettings.newHttpJsonBuilder()) and a container.* endpoint host.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
REST APIgcloud 
# Create a cluster (path mode)
curl -X POST \
  "http://localhost:4588/container/v1/projects/floci-local/locations/us-central1/clusters" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"cluster":{"name":"my-cluster"}}'

# Get / list clusters
curl "http://localhost:4588/container/v1/projects/floci-local/locations/us-central1/clusters/my-cluster"
curl "http://localhost:4588/container/v1/projects/floci-local/locations/us-central1/clusters"

# Delete a cluster
curl -X DELETE \
  "http://localhost:4588/container/v1/projects/floci-local/locations/us-central1/clusters/my-cluster"

export CLOUDSDK_API_ENDPOINT_OVERRIDES_CONTAINER="http://localhost:4588/container/"
# gcloud preflights an API-enablement check; point serviceusage at the emulator and
# disable the enable-API prompt (floci-gcp ignores auth).
export CLOUDSDK_API_ENDPOINT_OVERRIDES_SERVICEUSAGE="http://localhost:4588/"
export CLOUDSDK_CORE_SHOULD_PROMPT_TO_ENABLE_API=false

gcloud container clusters create my-cluster --region=us-central1 --async
gcloud container clusters list --region=us-central1

docs.title: kubectl Access
docs.text:
Real (non-mock) clusters run an actual k3s API server, so the native gcloud container clusters get-credentials + kubectl flow works end to end:

gcloud container clusters get-credentials my-cluster --region=us-central1
kubectl get nodes

get-credentials writes a kubeconfig that authenticates with the GCP access token produced by the gke-gcloud-auth-plugin. k3s forwards any bearer token it does not recognise to floci-gcp's token-authentication webhook. Because floci-gcp does not validate credentials, the webhook accepts any non-empty token and maps it to cluster-admin. The cluster endpoint is advertised as a reachable host:port (FLOCI_GCP_SERVICES_GKE_ENDPOINT_MODE=host, the default) so the kubeconfig server URL resolves correctly.

This flow requires a real cluster: it does not apply in mock mode, where no API server is started.

docs.title: Mock Mode
docs.text: Set FLOCI_GCP_SERVICES_GKE_MOCK=true to create clusters in memory that report RUNNING immediately without starting a k3s container. Useful for CI and for tools that provision a cluster but never connect to its API server.

docs.title: Node Pools
docs.text:
Node pools are modeled as real, independent resources (not a static field on the cluster): CreateCluster provisions a default-pool node pool from the request's top-level initialNodeCount/nodeConfig (or from an explicit nodePools[] list), and it can be deleted and replaced with separately-managed pools — the standard remove_default_node_pool = true + standalone google_container_node_pool pattern used by Terraform, OpenTofu, and Pulumi all work end to end.

config, autoscaling, management, upgradeSettings and placementPolicy are stored verbatim from the create/update request and echoed back unchanged on every read — floci-gcp does not run real node VMs or enforce autoscaling/repair/upgrade behavior, so there is nothing to act on semantically. This keeps every field a real client sends round-tripping consistently for Terraform's plan/refresh diff, without hand-modeling the full NodeConfig proto surface.

node_count drifts on every terraform plan unless you set ignore_node_count_changes

Real GKE's Terraform provider computes the live node_count value by querying Compute Engine Instance Group Manager target sizes for the node pool's instanceGroupUrls — not from any field the NodePool API itself returns. floci-gcp does not emulate Compute Engine, so instanceGroupUrls is always empty and the provider reads node_count back as 0, which it then wants to "correct" on every plan. Set ignore_node_count_changes = true on google_container_node_pool resources to skip that IGM-based read entirely and use initial_node_count as the source of truth instead (the provider's own documented escape hatch for exactly this situation).

docs.title: Supported Operations
docs.text:
• CreateCluster, GetCluster, ListClusters, DeleteCluster, UpdateCluster, UpdateMaster
  • SetResourceLabels, SetMasterAuth, SetNetworkPolicy, SetAddonsConfig, SetLoggingService, SetMonitoringService, SetLocations, SetLegacyAbac, SetMaintenancePolicy, StartIPRotation, CompleteIPRotation
  • CreateNodePool, GetNodePool, ListNodePools, DeleteNodePool, UpdateNodePool
  • SetNodePoolAutoscaling, SetNodePoolManagement, SetNodePoolSize, CompleteNodePoolUpgrade, RollbackNodePoolUpgrade
  • GetServerConfig, GetJSONWebKeys, ListUsableSubnetworks, CheckAutopilotCompatibility, FetchClusterUpgradeInfo, FetchNodePoolUpgradeInfo
  • GetOperation / ListOperations

ListClusters and ListOperations accept - as the location (projects/{project}/locations/-) to list across all zones and regions.

This is the full container.v1 ClusterManager RPC surface except CancelOperation (operations are always synchronous/DONE, so there is nothing in flight to cancel).

The five read-only RPCs above report honest stub data rather than fabricated analysis, since floci-gcp has no real infrastructure behind them to inspect:

  • GetJSONWebKeys returns an empty key set — floci-gcp accepts any bearer token (no real credential validation), so there is no real signing key to expose, and a fabricated one would misleadingly imply verifiable tokens are possible.
  • ListUsableSubnetworks returns the single synthetic "default" network/subnetwork every cluster in this emulator already defaults to — floci-gcp does not emulate Compute Engine/VPC, so there is no real subnetwork inventory.
  • CheckAutopilotCompatibility always reports no issues — there is no real policy engine to evaluate a cluster's configuration against.
  • FetchClusterUpgradeInfo/FetchNodePoolUpgradeInfo report the current version as both current and target with nothing pending — floci-gcp has a single fixed master/node version, so there is never a real upgrade path.
  • UpdateCluster with desiredNodeVersion upgrades the single node pool named by desiredNodePoolId, matching the real API, where that field is mandatory once a cluster has more than one pool. With exactly one pool the id may be omitted; with several it is required, and a request without it is rejected as 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT rather than silently upgrading pools the caller did not name. desiredMasterVersion and desiredNodeVersion accept the same aliases as UpdateMaster below, with the documented difference that - on the node side picks the cluster's current master version rather than the server default. This is what gcloud container clusters upgrade sends when no --cluster-version is given, so both forms of that command leave the cluster on a real version.
  • UpdateMaster moves only the control plane: currentMasterVersion changes and currentNodeVersion and every node pool's version stay as they were, as in real GKE, where the master and node pools upgrade independently. masterVersion is required (400 INVALID_ARGUMENT when missing). The aliases the API documents resolve against this emulator's single advertised version: latest, -, and a 1.X / 1.X.Y prefix of it all pick that version; any other explicit 1.X.Y-gke.N is stored verbatim, as CreateCluster and UpdateCluster already do. A 1.X / 1.X.Y alias that matches no valid version has nothing to pick and is rejected with 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT naming the field and the valid version, as is a value outside the five documented shapes (a bare 1, for example). The operation is reported as UPGRADE_MASTER, the Operation.Type real GKE uses.

Autopilot mode (autopilot.enabled) and Fleet/Anthos registration (fleet) are not semantically modeled — floci-gcp does not run a real Autopilot node-management control loop or register with a real Fleet — but both round-trip correctly through extraConfig like every other config block the emulator doesn't act on, so tooling that merely checks cluster.autopilot.enabled or cluster.fleet.project works correctly.

All mutations return a synchronous, DONE Operation (no real long-running operation lifecycle) — consistent across every RPC above, not just cluster create/delete as before. The one exception is CompleteNodePoolUpgrade, which returns google.protobuf.Empty ({}) as the real API does.

StartIPRotation/CompleteIPRotation acknowledge the request (bumping the cluster's fingerprint/etag) rather than performing a real dual-certificate rotation window — there is no live client traffic to migrate off an old certificate in this emulator. CompleteNodePoolUpgrade/RollbackNodePoolUpgrade validate the node pool exists, then return {} and an Operation respectively; there is no real node-version upgrade in flight to complete or roll back, since node pools don't run real node VMs. GetServerConfig reports this emulator's single supported master/node version across all three release channels (RAPID/REGULAR/STABLE) — there is no real multi-version fleet behind it.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Operations resolve synchronously (no real long-running operation lifecycle, no CancelOperation).
  • Node IAM is not modeled.
  • Real Autopilot node management and Compute Engine-backed node scaling (node_count read-back — see the warning above) are out of scope; floci-gcp does not run real node VMs, so Autopilot mode and Fleet registration round-trip as config but are not semantically enforced.
  • Cluster-level config blocks the emulator doesn't act on semantically (network policy enforcement, binary authorization, private cluster networking, etc.) are stored and echoed back verbatim rather than enforced — see the config/autoscaling/management note under Node Pools above, which applies at the cluster level too (extraConfig).

docs.title: IAM Service Account Credentials
docs.text:
floci-gcp emulates the IAM Service Account Credentials API (iamcredentials.googleapis.com v1) with REST JSON, supporting generateAccessToken, signBlob and signJwt for service-account impersonation flows (for example ImpersonatedCredentials in the GCP SDKs, which call signBlob to make GCS signed URLs).

The endpoint returns an opaque emulator token (floci-gcp-impersonated-<uuid>) that the supported IAM-enforcing services resolve to a service-account identity. With FLOCI_GCP_SERVICES_IAM_AUTHORIZATION_MODE=enforce, a recognized caller needs iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken on the target account, including applicable project policies. Signing requires iam.serviceAccounts.signBlob or iam.serviceAccounts.signJwt respectively. See the method and role inventory. Anonymous/external credentials bypass this evaluation, including bootstrap token issuance. Tokens are local emulator credentials and cannot be used with real GCP.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Variable Default Description FLOCI_GCP_SERVICES_IAMCREDENTIALS_ENABLED true Enable or disable the IAM Credentials service

docs.title: Endpoint
docs.text:
POST /v1/projects/-/serviceAccounts/{serviceAccount}:generateAccessToken

Request body:

Field Behavior scope Required. Must include at least one of https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform or https://www.googleapis.com/auth/devstorage.read_write; a request containing neither is rejected with INVALID_ARGUMENT lifetime Optional "<n>s" duration string. Defaults to 3600s; values above 3600s are capped; non-positive values are rejected delegates Empty or omitted for direct requests. Non-empty chains are unsupported and fail with FAILED_PRECONDITION for evaluated callers in enforce mode; bypass/disabled callers retain the previous ignored behavior

Response: { "accessToken": "...", "expireTime": "..." }.

POST /v1/projects/-/serviceAccounts/{serviceAccount}:signBlob
POST /v1/projects/-/serviceAccounts/{serviceAccount}:signJwt

Both sign with the service account's Google-managed RSA-2048 key (see Sign Blob); the account must exist, or the call fails with PERMISSION_DENIED.

Method Request Response signBlob payload: base64 bytes { "keyId", "signedBlob" }, an RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5 SHA-256 signature signJwt payload: a JSON object of JWT claims; an exp claim must be an integer timestamp, not in the past and at most 12 hours ahead { "keyId", "signedJwt" }, an RS256 JWT whose header carries kid

IAM v1 serviceAccounts.signBlob uses the same path when the project is -; a request that sends bytesToSign instead of payload is answered in the IAM v1 shape. Because that path is served here, it returns UNAVAILABLE while the IAM Credentials service is disabled.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
ImpersonatedCredentials credentials = ImpersonatedCredentials.newBuilder()
    .setSourceCredentials(sourceCredentials)
    .setTargetPrincipal("my-sa@floci-local.iam.gserviceaccount.com")
    .setScopes(List.of("https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"))
    .setLifetime(3600)
    .setIamEndpointOverride("http://localhost:4588")
    .build();

docs.title: Not Yet Supported
docs.text:
• generateIdToken
  • Scope-based authorization of the vended token (the supported IAM evaluator checks identity and policies, not OAuth scopes)
  • Delegation chains (only direct impersonation is IAM-enforced)

docs.title: IAM
docs.text: floci-gcp emulates Google Cloud IAM over REST JSON and the shared IAM policy gRPC mixin.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Variable Default Description FLOCI_GCP_SERVICES_IAM_ENABLED true Enable/disable IAM FLOCI_GCP_SERVICES_IAM_AUTHORIZATION_MODE disabled Set to enforce to evaluate allow policies for the supported services below FLOCI_GCP_SERVICES_IAM_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_MEMBER unset Optional IAM member granted roles/storage.admin on each newly created bucket

docs.title: Opt-in enforcement
docs.text:
Set FLOCI_GCP_SERVICES_IAM_AUTHORIZATION_MODE=enforce, or floci-gcp.services.iam.authorization-mode: enforce in YAML. The default is disabled: stored policies do not restrict requests. Startup logs always report which mode is active and the supported service list.

Surface IAM enforcement in enforce mode Resource Manager v1 project metadata and project policies REST JSON; project policies also use the shared IAM gRPC mixin Cloud Billing v1 project billing info REST JSON GET only; the PUT update is not evaluated. See Cloud Billing IAM enforcement Cloud Run v2 services and revisions REST JSON service and revision operations; service-policy methods also use the shared IAM gRPC API. See Cloud Run IAM enforcement GCS buckets Supported REST bucket metadata, IAM-policy, retention-lock, storage-layout, and notification operations; bucket testIamPermissions filters its response GCS objects Supported REST JSON and XML reads, writes, updates, deletes, listing, compose, copy, rewrite, move, restore, resumable uploads, and XML multipart uploads Pub/Sub REST JSON and gRPC topic, subscription, snapshot, and policy methods; testIamPermissions filters its response Cloud Scheduler REST JSON and gRPC job create/get/list/update/delete/pause/resume/run; project policy inheritance. See Scheduler IAM enforcement Secret Manager REST JSON and gRPC secret and version operations; see Secret Manager IAM enforcement IAM service accounts and keys REST JSON service-account CRUD, key management, IAM policy methods over REST and shared IAM gRPC, signBlob, and IAM Credentials generateAccessToken, signBlob, and signJwt IAM custom roles REST JSON project and organization role create, get, list, patch, delete, and undelete. Bindings to stored custom roles grant their includedPermissions on every surface above except GCS bucket policies. See Custom roles GCS ACLs and GCS gRPC Not IAM-enforced. Existing downscoped-token CAB checks still apply IAM Credentials generateIdToken, Cloud Run jobs, worker pools, instances, invocation and operations, all other services Not IAM-enforced, including any policies those services store

Valid Floci-issued service-account tokens activate IAM evaluation on every supported surface. Mint one through the existing IAM Credentials generateAccessToken endpoint and pass it as Authorization: Bearer TOKEN or through your SDK credentials provider. For plaintext gRPC, Google credentials may refuse an insecure channel before the request reaches the emulator; use a fixed authorization header with the SDK's no-credentials provider, or use the emulator's TLS transport. Anonymous requests and external credentials bypass Resource Manager, Cloud Run, Secret Manager, Pub/Sub, and IAM service-account evaluation. GCS evaluation treats those callers as anonymous so allUsers policies work. In enforce mode, an unknown or expired Floci-issued token receives UNAUTHENTICATED; an evaluated caller without a matching grant receives 403 PERMISSION_DENIED over REST or PERMISSION_DENIED over gRPC. GCS applies the Credential Access Boundary before IAM and retains the source principal for IAM evaluation of valid downscoped credentials. Downscoped tokens cannot expand their boundary into project or bucket management permissions.

This is a local permission-testing tool, not an authentication/security boundary. Anonymous or external callers can still mint emulator credentials because those identities bypass policy evaluation. A test using such credentials can pass without exercising IAM.

The framework supports child-to-project inheritance and multiple required permission checks. Bucket evaluation includes the owning project's policy; the project cannot be inferred from the projects/_/buckets/... resource name and is read from the stored bucket metadata. Pub/Sub resources, Cloud Run services, and Secret Manager secrets inherit their project policy. Project bindings do not authorize or restrict other services without a registered adapter. testIamPermissions evaluates each requested permission for the same caller and resource; missing resources keep the existing empty-result behavior. Disabled mode and bypass callers retain the existing permission echo.

Bucket policies inherit to objects. Restore requires storage.objects.restore and storage.objects.create, plus storage.objects.delete when it replaces a live object. Move accepts storage.objects.move on the source, or both storage.objects.get and storage.objects.delete, and requires storage.objects.create on the destination. Resumable-upload permissions are established when the session is opened; the session URI then acts as the authorization token for status queries and chunks, including requests without an Authorization header.

XML multipart upload IDs are not authentication tokens. Every initiate, part upload, completion, list, list-parts, and abort request evaluates its documented storage.multipartUploads.* permission. Uploading parts and completing an upload also require storage.objects.create; completion requires storage.objects.delete when it replaces a live object.

For a downscoped token derived from a Floci-issued IAM Credentials impersonated token, Floci preserves the source service-account identity. Object requests first satisfy the token's Credential Access Boundary (CAB), then satisfy the bucket policy for that service account. Consequently, a bucket policy cannot extend a CAB grant, and a CAB cannot extend a bucket-policy grant. A downscoped token from an external source credential has no named IAM identity and, in enforce mode, can match only an allUsers binding.

docs.title: Bucket enforcement bootstrap
docs.text:
When Floci can resolve a new bucket's caller from a valid Floci-issued impersonated token, it persists a bucket-level roles/storage.admin binding for that service-account member. This lets the creator manage the bucket after the emulator is started with authorization-mode: enforce.

For callers without a resolvable identity, set FLOCI_GCP_SERVICES_IAM_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_MEMBER to an IAM member such as serviceAccount:admin@example.iam.gserviceaccount.com. That member receives roles/storage.admin on every subsequently created bucket. Treat this setting as an administrator credential: it is deliberately powerful, and an allUsers value makes every new bucket publicly manageable. The setting accepts only serviceAccount: members, allAuthenticatedUsers, or allUsers.

docs.title: Supported roles and conditions
docs.text:
The finite catalog includes the implemented-operation permissions from:

  • roles/browser and roles/resourcemanager.projectIamAdmin.
  • roles/owner, roles/editor, and roles/viewer, restricted to the declared service permissions. Editor/viewer permit project metadata and policy reads, but not project policy writes.

In enforce mode, project policies cannot contain allUsers or allAuthenticatedUsers. Such bindings produce INVALID_ARGUMENT on policy writes and when evaluating previously stored project policies. Disabled mode retains permissive policy storage.

The finite catalog also contains roles/storage.objectViewer, roles/storage.objectCreator, roles/storage.objectUser, roles/storage.objectAdmin, and roles/storage.admin for the explicitly enforced bucket and object permissions. Secret Manager roles, permission targets, and inheritance are described in the Secret Manager guide. Uncatalogued roles grant no permissions and do not block known bindings, including when they apply to the caller. Missing resource/operation mappings on an enforcing adapter produce a named FAILED_PRECONDITION. The shared google.iam.v1.IAMPolicy gRPC mixin enforces project, service-account, Cloud Run service, Secret Manager secret, and Pub/Sub topic, subscription, and snapshot policy resources. It rejects resource kinds without a registered mapping for recognized callers in enforce mode. Those policy APIs support anonymous setup calls. Unsupported CEL expressions produce INVALID_ARGUMENT; they are not silently treated as a policy denial.

Version 3 bindings use the existing restricted IAM Conditions profile, including resource service/type/name, string comparisons and prefixes, logical operators, and request-time comparison. The CEL standard library is not enabled. The catalog and condition profile are subsets of Google Cloud IAM.

Cloud Logging GCS sinks authorize fresh object creation as their persisted writer principal, including bucket/project policy grants and supported conditions. They do not use the logging caller's credentials. See GCS export. Sink management authorization is not implemented.

docs.title: Service-account enforcement
docs.text:
The following inventory covers the implemented IAM v1 REST methods. Links point at the exact Google API method contract. P is projects/{project}; SA is P/serviceAccounts/{email}; K is SA/keys/{key}.

Method Required permission Authorization target Implemented transport create iam.serviceAccounts.create P REST POST list iam.serviceAccounts.list P REST GET get iam.serviceAccounts.get SA REST GET update, patch iam.serviceAccounts.update SA REST PUT, PATCH delete iam.serviceAccounts.delete SA REST DELETE keys.create iam.serviceAccountKeys.create SA REST POST keys.list iam.serviceAccountKeys.list SA REST GET keys.get iam.serviceAccountKeys.get K REST GET keys.delete iam.serviceAccountKeys.delete K REST DELETE getIamPolicy iam.serviceAccounts.getIamPolicy SA REST POST, shared IAM v1 gRPC setIamPolicy iam.serviceAccounts.setIamPolicy SA REST POST, shared IAM v1 gRPC testIamPermissions No prerequisite permission; filters requested permissions through the evaluator SA REST POST, shared IAM v1 gRPC signBlob iam.serviceAccounts.signBlob SA IAM v1 REST POST generateAccessToken iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken SA IAM Credentials v1 REST POST Credentials signBlob iam.serviceAccounts.signBlob SA IAM Credentials v1 REST POST Credentials signJwt iam.serviceAccounts.signJwt SA IAM Credentials v1 REST POST

Service-account policies and project policies participate in each account/key check. Key operations use the account's policy and owning project, with the key name as the evaluation target for get/delete. Account IDs, unique IDs, and the projects/- wildcard resolve through the existing service-account resolver to a canonical email policy key. Authorization resolves names without migrating policies. When the canonical email policy is absent, it reads legacy account-ID, unique-ID, and wildcard-address policies without changing their keys. An existing canonical policy takes precedence, including an empty policy. Policy methods may subsequently adopt legacy policy keys using the existing migration path.

Creation and deletion clear the account's direct policies, including legacy aliases. Account updates, policy writes, migration, and these lifecycle transitions use ordered policy locks, so an update cannot republish a deleted account and a replacement cannot inherit its previous direct policy. Policy reads and writes require an existing account. Permission tests on missing accounts addressed by project ID return an empty permission list, following the shared IAM policy contract. This implements the local resource boundary; Google treats a recreated service account as a separate identity. Floci's email-based principal matching does not reproduce Google's deleted-principal and undelete lifecycle.

The Google IAM roles and permissions reference defines these finite role slices for the implemented permissions:

Role Supported IAM permission slice roles/iam.serviceAccountAdmin Service-account create, get, list, update, delete, getIamPolicy, setIamPolicy roles/iam.serviceAccountKeyAdmin Key create, get, list, delete; service-account get, list roles/iam.serviceAccountUser Service-account get, list; actAs is not an implemented operation roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator Service-account get, list, getAccessToken, signBlob, signJwt roles/viewer Service-account get, list, getIamPolicy; key get, list roles/editor Viewer slice plus service-account create, update, delete and key create, delete roles/owner Editor slice plus service-account setIamPolicy

Each listed predefined IAM role also contributes resourcemanager.projects.get for the supported Resource Manager adapter. Basic roles do not grant getAccessToken, signBlob, or signJwt. These are explicit slices of Google's roles, not the full production role catalog.

The local evaluator exposes resource.service = 'iam.googleapis.com', resource.type = 'iam.googleapis.com/ServiceAccount' (or iam.googleapis.com/Key), and canonical email-based resource.name values. Create/list use the project attributes. Supported equality, prefix, and logical conditions use the shared condition subset. Google does not document these IAM resource attributes in its supported resource attribute table. Treat this as local scope-testing behavior, not proof that the same expression or alias representation works in production. Exact GCP condition evaluation, error messages/metadata, and revocation timing have not been verified live.

Authorization happens in the shared REST filter or gRPC interceptor before the controller invokes an operation. Denied management requests must leave accounts, keys, and policies unchanged; denied credential requests must not issue a token or signing response. The existing filters do not hold policy locks across the subsequent mutation, so they provide no atomic policy-revocation guarantee.

Service-account enable, disable, undelete, key upload, enable/disable, IAM v1 signJwt, and Credentials generateIdToken are unimplemented. Only the shared IAM policy gRPC mixin is exposed; IAM admin and IAM Credentials gRPC services are not implemented. Non-empty credential delegation chains fail with FAILED_PRECONDITION for evaluated callers; disabled and bypass callers retain the existing permissive behavior. IAM permissions alone do not define a fixed list of roles a caller may grant; Organization Policy constraints for limiting grants are unsupported.

docs.title: Custom roles
docs.text:
The IAM v1 projects.roles and organizations.roles REST methods create, read, and manage custom roles. R is projects/{project}/roles/{role} or organizations/{organization}/roles/{role}; P is its parent.

Method Required permission Authorization target Implemented transport create iam.roles.create P REST POST /v1/{P}/roles list iam.roles.list P REST GET /v1/{P}/roles get iam.roles.get R REST GET /v1/{R} patch iam.roles.update R REST PATCH /v1/{R} delete iam.roles.delete R REST DELETE /v1/{R} undelete iam.roles.undelete R REST POST /v1/{R}:undelete

Role targets evaluate their parent's allow policy. The local evaluator exposes resource.type = 'iam.googleapis.com/Role' and the role name for conditions; create and list use the parent's attributes. Organization targets read the policy stored under organizations/{organization}. Resource Manager organization policy methods are not implemented, so evaluated callers are denied organization-role management unless an organization policy was stored through the shared IAM policy gRPC mixin, which accepts organization names only from anonymous and external callers.

The Google IAM roles and permissions reference defines these slices:

Role Supported permission slice roles/iam.roleAdmin, roles/iam.organizationRoleAdmin iam.roles.create, delete, get, list, undelete, update; resourcemanager.projects.get, getIamPolicy roles/iam.roleViewer, roles/iam.organizationRoleViewer iam.roles.get, list; resourcemanager.projects.get, getIamPolicy

roles/owner also holds all six iam.roles.* permissions; roles/editor and roles/viewer hold iam.roles.get and iam.roles.list, matching gcloud iam roles describe.

docs.title: Role definitions
docs.text:
Roles are persisted with the configured storage mode under their full resource name. Create takes the roleId and role fields of the request. Limits and validation follow GCP:

  • Role IDs are 3 to 64 letters, digits, underscores, or periods.
  • The title is limited to 100 UTF-8 bytes, the description to 300, and the role to 3,000 permissions, counting duplicates.
  • Permissions containing * are rejected. Other permissions are stored as sent: GCP also rejects unknown and organization-only permissions with 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT Permission X is not valid., which Floci cannot check without a full permission catalog.
  • stage defaults to ALPHA, which responses omit. includedPermissions also accepts a single string.

List returns the BASIC view without includedPermissions unless view=FULL, hides deleted roles unless showDeleted=true, and pages 300 roles by default; a pageSize above 1,000 or below zero is rejected. Patch applies updateMask (title, description, includedPermissions, stage) or, without a mask, replaces all four and clears the fields absent from the request. A name in the patch body must equal the path. Delete marks the role deleted and undelete restores it; deleted roles are never purged, so their IDs stay reserved.

Error codes: duplicate IDs return ALREADY_EXISTS; reusing a deleted role's ID, updating or deleting a deleted role, and undeleting an active one return FAILED_PRECONDITION; unknown roles return NOT_FOUND; a mismatched etag on update, delete, or undelete returns ABORTED. On a deleted role, update reports the stale etag first and delete reports the deleted state first; undelete reports an active role before a stale etag. These codes and messages, including those for malformed or non-string etags, out-of-range page sizes, invalid update masks and role names, and fields of the wrong JSON type, were checked against GCP. Two cases were not observed: a non-string includedPermissions entry reuses Permission X is not valid., and a malformed etag in a patch body reuses the malformed-etag message. Denial messages use the shared enforcement text, not GCP's per-method wording. Predefined GET /v1/roles and the IAM admin gRPC role methods are not implemented.

docs.title: Effective permissions
docs.text:
A binding to a custom role grants exactly the role's stored includedPermissions, under the same conditions as any other binding, for every operation an enforcing adapter checks. Defining a role does not implement an operation.

  • A project role grants only through allow policies stored on that project or on resources whose names are under projects/{project}/.
  • An organization role grants through policies of projects whose recorded Resource Manager parent is that organization (parent.type organization). Its own organization policy is evaluated only for organization-role management; organization policies do not inherit to projects.
  • GCS bucket policies have no project in their resource name, so custom-role bindings in bucket policies grant nothing. Bindings on the owning project's policy still apply to its buckets.
  • Missing, DISABLED, and deleted roles grant nothing. Edits, disabling, deletion, and undeletion apply to the next authorization decision for existing bindings and credentials, and survive restarts with persistent storage. GCP applied each of these within about a second in live checks.

docs.title: Project identity and ancestry
docs.text:
• A project policy is stored and evaluated under the project ID: projects/{number} of a known project reads, writes and inherits the same policy as projects/{id}, over REST and the shared IAM gRPC mixin. Role names and other resource policy keys keep the project segment as sent, so a role under projects/{number} and its project ID name different stored roles, and a role under projects/{number} does not grant through project policies. Organization roles grant only through policies keyed by a project ID.
  • Organization role requests name no project, so Service Usage gates them on the request's project context, which is the default project unless the request names one.
  • Folder and organization ancestry is modelled only as a project's direct parent. Projects without a parent, projects under a folder, and unknown projects grant nothing for organization roles, although GCP lets projects under a folder use their organization's roles.
  • The recorded parent is set by Resource Manager update, which checks only resourcemanager.projects.update on the project, and by a create that adopts a project first registered implicitly, which checks only resourcemanager.projects.create. Neither checks a permission on the destination, so moving a project under an organization activates that organization's roles in bindings the project already holds.
  • A project in DELETE_REQUESTED keeps its custom roles: they can still be managed and still grant, and its recorded parent still scopes organization roles.

docs.title: Policy writes
docs.text:
In enforce mode, setIamPolicy on a resource with an enforcing adapter (projects, Pub/Sub topics, subscriptions and snapshots, Secret Manager secrets, Cloud Run services, and service accounts, over REST and the shared IAM gRPC API) checks each role-member grant that is not already in the stored policy and rejects it with 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT when it binds:

  • a custom role defined in another project, or an organization role in a project whose recorded parent is another organization or that was created without a parent: Role (NAME) does not exist in the resource's hierarchy.
  • a custom role that does not exist: Role (NAME) does not exist in resource's hierarchy.
  • a deleted custom role: Cannot add new grants to deleted role (NAME).

Grants already in the stored policy are kept, so bindings to a role deleted later stay in the policy and grant nothing. Placements the emulator cannot decide are accepted: organization roles in projects under a folder, in projects registered implicitly, or in unknown projects, and project numbers that are not registered. Predefined roles are not checked. In disabled mode, and for resources without an enforcing adapter (GCS bucket policies, Cloud Functions, Cloud Run jobs, worker pools and instances, organization policies), all bindings are stored as sent.

A binding to a missing, deleted, or disabled custom role is skipped without checking its condition. Creating, undeleting, or enabling that role makes the binding apply, and an unsupported condition on it then fails the member's evaluated requests on that policy with INVALID_ARGUMENT until the binding is removed by a caller that bypasses evaluation or the role is disabled again.

OAuth /token, STS exchanges, and metadata credentials retain their existing emulator behavior. OAuth's stub exchange does not authenticate a service-account JWT; its token is not a recognized service-account identity. Anonymous/external credential bypass makes this emulator a local testing tool, not a security boundary. IAM v1 signBlob returns the keyId and signature fields required by its contract. IAM v1 and Credentials signing share the emulator's per-account RSA key described in Sign Blob. This is a local key, not a Google-managed production credential.

docs.title: Remaining limitations
docs.text:
• Object-list conditions authorize the bucket-level storage.objects.list permission but do not filter returned objects.
  • GCS gRPC and ACL operations are not restricted by IAM allow policies. Signed-URL identity is also outside the evaluator: because the emulator does not cryptographically verify V4 signatures, signed URLs are treated as anonymous and can access only resources granted to allUsers in enforce mode.
  • Conditional GCS bindings require UBLA. A bucket update cannot disable, remove, or partially clear UBLA while conditional bindings remain configured. The full UBLA lifecycle is not implemented.
  • Organization/folder inheritance, deny policies, principal access boundaries, group/domain membership expansion, workforce/workload identities, and organization policy constraints are not implemented.
  • Service-account address aliases resolve to canonical email policy names, and a known project's number resolves to its project ID for project policies. Other resource names are evaluated as requested, so projects/{number}/... child resources keep their own policy keys.
  • Only declared operation permissions are checked. Dependent service-agent, actAs, push-authentication, BigQuery export, CMEK, and other cross-service grants are not validated. This emulator cannot prove those configurations work in GCP.
  • Shared REST/gRPC interceptors do not hold policy locks through business mutations. GCS object operations and Logging GCS export use service-level locks through publication; other integrations must provide their own consistency boundary.
  • The emulator does not validate that a predefined role is grantable on the policy resource. Custom-role bindings are checked as described in Policy writes. Unsupported permissions in a known role are absent from the catalog.

See Adding an enforcing service for the shared extension contract, test requirements, and upstream evidence.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
gcloud CLIREST API 
gcloud config set project floci-local

# Create a service account
gcloud iam service-accounts create my-sa \
    --display-name="My Service Account"

# List service accounts
gcloud iam service-accounts list

# Create a key
gcloud iam service-accounts keys create key.json \
    --iam-account=my-sa@floci-local.iam.gserviceaccount.com

# Delete a key
gcloud iam service-accounts keys delete KEY_ID \
    --iam-account=my-sa@floci-local.iam.gserviceaccount.com

# Create service account
curl -X POST http://localhost:4588/v1/projects/floci-local/serviceAccounts \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"accountId":"my-sa","serviceAccount":{"displayName":"My SA"}}'

# List service accounts
curl http://localhost:4588/v1/projects/floci-local/serviceAccounts

# Get service account
curl http://localhost:4588/v1/projects/floci-local/serviceAccounts/my-sa@floci-local.iam.gserviceaccount.com

# Delete service account
curl -X DELETE http://localhost:4588/v1/projects/floci-local/serviceAccounts/my-sa@floci-local.iam.gserviceaccount.com

docs.title: Service Accounts
docs.text:
Service accounts follow the GCP naming convention:

projects/{project}/serviceAccounts/{account}@{project}.iam.gserviceaccount.com

The - wildcard can replace the project ID in any service account or key name (projects/-/serviceAccounts/{EMAIL_ADDRESS|UNIQUE_ID}), which is what Terraform sends. The owning project is resolved from the account, and resource names in responses carry the real project. As on GCP, a missing account addressed through - returns 403 PERMISSION_DENIED instead of 404 NOT_FOUND.

docs.title: Service Account Keys
docs.text:
# Create key
curl -X POST \
  http://localhost:4588/v1/projects/floci-local/serviceAccounts/my-sa@floci-local.iam.gserviceaccount.com/keys \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{}'

# List keys
curl http://localhost:4588/v1/projects/floci-local/serviceAccounts/my-sa@floci-local.iam.gserviceaccount.com/keys

docs.title: IAM Policy Bindings
docs.text:
# Grant Secret Manager access to a service account
gcloud secrets add-iam-policy-binding my-secret \
    --member="serviceAccount:my-sa@floci-local.iam.gserviceaccount.com" \
    --role="roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor"

docs.title: Sign Blob (V4 Signed URLs)
docs.text:
The IAM SignBlob endpoint is used by the GCS SDK to generate V4 pre-signed URLs:

URL signedUrl = storage.signUrl(
    BlobInfo.newBuilder("my-bucket", "hello.txt").build(),
    15, TimeUnit.MINUTES,
    Storage.SignUrlOption.withV4Signature());

SignBlob ({"bytesToSign": "<base64>"}) returns {"keyId", "signature"}: an RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5 SHA-256 signature made with the service account's Google-managed RSA-2048 key. Each account gets one such key the first time it signs, kept until the account is deleted, and the same key signs for the IAM Credentials signBlob and signJwt methods.

The signing key is not returned by ListServiceAccountKeys (real IAM lists it as a SYSTEM_MANAGED key), so its public half cannot be read back and signatures cannot be verified against it locally. Nothing in floci-gcp verifies them: GCS checks a signed URL's expiry, not its signature.

docs.title: Cloud KMS
docs.text: floci-gcp emulates Google Cloud KMS over gRPC and REST using the real google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService protocol. Crypto operations are backed by real local cryptography (AES-256-GCM for symmetric keys; RSA/EC for asymmetric keys; HMAC for MAC keys), so encrypt/decrypt, sign/verify and MAC sign/verify round-trips behave like GCP, including binding ciphertext to the key version, so a cross-key decrypt fails as it would in production.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Variable Default Description FLOCI_GCP_SERVICES_KMS_ENABLED true Enable/disable Cloud KMS

docs.title: Endpoint
docs.text:
Cloud KMS has no *_EMULATOR_HOST convention. Point the client at floci-gcp by overriding the API endpoint / transport channel and disabling credentials:

  • gRPC (Java/Python/Go/Node): build the client with a plaintext channel to localhost:4588 and anonymous/no credentials (see Quick Start below).
  • REST / Terraform: set the provider's kms_custom_endpoint to http://localhost:4588/v1/.

docs.title: Supported algorithms
docs.text:
Purpose Algorithm Operations ENCRYPT_DECRYPT GOOGLE_SYMMETRIC_ENCRYPTION (AES-256-GCM) Encrypt, Decrypt ASYMMETRIC_SIGN EC_SIGN_P256_SHA256, RSA_SIGN_PKCS1_2048_SHA256 AsymmetricSign, GetPublicKey ASYMMETRIC_DECRYPT RSA_DECRYPT_OAEP_2048_SHA256 AsymmetricDecrypt, GetPublicKey MAC HMAC_SHA256, HMAC_SHA1, HMAC_SHA384, HMAC_SHA512, HMAC_SHA224 MacSign, MacVerify

A MAC key needs version_template.algorithm, like an ASYMMETRIC_SIGN key. Each version holds a random HMAC key the size of its hash output (32 bytes for HMAC_SHA256). MacVerify returns success: false for a tag that does not match, whatever its length, rather than an error, and sets verified_success_integrity to the same value as success.

docs.title: Quick Start
Key Versions
docs.text:
CreateCryptoKey with ENCRYPT_DECRYPT auto-creates version 1 and marks it primary. Encrypt uses the primary version unless a specific version is named; Decrypt automatically selects the version that produced the ciphertext. Rotate by calling CreateCryptoKeyVersion then UpdateCryptoKeyPrimaryVersion. Version state transitions:

  • Enable/disable via UpdateCryptoKeyVersion (state = ENABLED / DISABLED).
  • DestroyCryptoKeyVersion moves a version to DESTROY_SCHEDULED; RestoreCryptoKeyVersion returns it to DISABLED. Crypto operations on a non-ENABLED version fail with FAILED_PRECONDITION.

docs.title: Key Settings
docs.text:
CreateCryptoKey stores labels, rotation_period, next_rotation_time and destroy_scheduled_duration, and every read returns them. A key created without destroy_scheduled_duration reports the 30 day default (2592000s). As the proto requires, rotation_period and next_rotation_time are accepted only on ENCRYPT_DECRYPT keys, rotation_period must be between 24 and 876,000 hours, and next_rotation_time must be set with it; anything else is INVALID_ARGUMENT.

UpdateCryptoKey applies the fields its update mask names (labels, rotation_period, next_rotation_time, version_template.algorithm); a named field left out of the request is cleared. Without a mask it applies the fields the request sets.

Deviations:

  • Keys are never rotated automatically: next_rotation_time is stored and returned, but no version is created when it passes.
  • destroy_scheduled_duration is not validated against a range, and DestroyCryptoKeyVersion does not use it yet: destroy_time is still the time of the call.
  • Update mask paths floci does not support, including immutable fields such as destroy_scheduled_duration and purpose, are ignored rather than rejected.
  • The INVALID_ARGUMENT messages are floci's own; production's wording was not verified.

docs.title: Integrity (CRC32C)
docs.text: Requests may include *_crc32c checksums (e.g. plaintext_crc32c); when present, floci-gcp verifies them and sets the corresponding verified_*_crc32c response flag (a mismatch yields INVALID_ARGUMENT). Responses always populate output checksums such as ciphertext_crc32c.

docs.title: Importing Keys
docs.text:
Bring-your-own-key imports follow the GCP import flow: create an ImportJob, wrap the key material with its public key, and import it into a CryptoKey, usually one created with import_only and skip_initial_version_creation.

Import method Wrapped key format RSA_OAEP_3072_SHA1_AES_256, RSA_OAEP_4096_SHA1_AES_256 RSA-OAEP (SHA-1, MGF1 SHA-1) of an ephemeral AES-256 key, followed by the target key wrapped with AES-KWP (RFC 5649) RSA_OAEP_3072_SHA256_AES_256, RSA_OAEP_4096_SHA256_AES_256 Same, with SHA-256 for OAEP and MGF1 RSA_OAEP_3072_SHA256, RSA_OAEP_4096_SHA256 The target key encrypted directly with RSA-OAEP (SHA-256)

Target key material is the raw 32 bytes for GOOGLE_SYMMETRIC_ENCRYPTION and a PKCS#8 DER private key for the asymmetric algorithms listed above. The public key of an imported asymmetric version is derived from the private key.

Behavior to be aware of:

  • Import jobs are ACTIVE as soon as they are created (no PENDING_GENERATION phase) and EXPIRED three days later; no attestation is returned for HSM jobs. As on GCP, an expired job no longer returns its public_key and reports expire_event_time instead.
  • Imports complete synchronously. Wrapped material that cannot be unwrapped, or that does not fit the requested algorithm, produces a version in IMPORT_FAILED with import_failure_reason set rather than an error.
  • The first successfully imported version of an ENCRYPT_DECRYPT key with no primary becomes the primary.
  • CreateCryptoKeyVersion on an import_only key fails with FAILED_PRECONDITION.
  • Re-importing into an existing version (crypto_key_version) is not supported.

docs.title: Locations
docs.text: Every regional GCP API also serves the google.cloud.location.Locations mixin (locations.proto). floci-gcp answers it from one bundled catalog of real GCP locations: 43 regions and their 130 zones, taken from Regions and zones. The same catalog drives Compute Engine regions and zones, and the optional strict location check described below.

docs.title: Endpoints
Which locations each caller sees
docs.text:
On a single port, the path does not say which API is being called. For REST, floci-gcp reads the first label of the Host header. A client that reaches floci-gcp under the real hostname (for example through the embedded DNS and TLS on port 443) gets the exact list for that API:

Host Locations Metadata cloudkms.* catalog regions, global, us, europe, asia google.cloud.kms.v1.LocationMetadata with hsmAvailable and ekmAvailable set to false, because the emulator keeps software keys only cloudfunctions.* catalog regions google.cloud.functions.v2.LocationMetadata with environments: ["GEN_2"] run.*, cloudtasks.*, cloudscheduler.*, eventarc.*, managedkafka.*, secretmanager.* catalog regions none

Every other caller gets the catalog regions plus KMS's four extra locations, with no metadata. That covers gRPC (the gRPC bridge does not expose the call authority) and any REST host that names no API, such as localhost or a Docker service name, which is what endpoint overrides usually send. KMS clients need those four locations, so the others see them too: for example, gcloud run regions list through an endpoint override lists global, us, europe and asia, which Cloud Run does not accept in strict mode.

docs.title: Strict location validation
docs.text:
By default floci-gcp accepts any location string, as it always has. Set FLOCI_GCP_LOCATIONS_STRICT=true (floci-gcp.locations.strict) to reject unknown locations with INVALID_ARGUMENT (Invalid location: {location}). Google does not document the exact error text, so this wording is floci-gcp's own.

API Checked on Accepted locations Cloud Run v2 service, job, worker pool, instance create and list catalog regions Cloud Functions v2 function create, function list catalog regions Cloud KMS key ring create, key ring list catalog regions, global, us, europe, asia Cloud Tasks queue create, queue list catalog regions Cloud Scheduler job create, job list catalog regions Eventarc trigger create, trigger list catalog regions Managed Kafka cluster create, cluster list catalog regions GKE cluster create, cluster list catalog regions and zones

The - list wildcard is never checked. Strict mode does not accept KMS dual-regional locations such as nam-eur-asia1 yet, because the bundled reference does not list them. Compute Engine does not use this setting. It always answers 404 for a region or zone that is not configured.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Variable Default Description FLOCI_GCP_LOCATIONS_STRICT false Reject unknown locations on regional create and list calls FLOCI_GCP_SERVICES_COMPUTE_REGIONS (unset) Optional Compute Engine region allow-list. Unset means the full catalog

The Locations endpoints are always on. They are not tied to any service's enabled flag.

docs.title: Cloud Logging
docs.text: floci-gcp emulates Google Cloud Logging over gRPC and REST using the real google.logging.v2.LoggingServiceV2 and sink-management methods of google.logging.v2.ConfigServiceV2. The primary use case is asserting what the app under test logged: write structured entries, then ListLogEntries back with a filter and verify the payload, severity, and resource.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Variable Default Description FLOCI_GCP_SERVICES_LOGGING_ENABLED true Enable/disable Cloud Logging

When disabled, sink management is unavailable: the gRPC ConfigServiceV2 API is not bound and returns UNIMPLEMENTED, while REST sink requests return HTTP 503 with UNAVAILABLE. Existing sink configurations remain stored.

docs.title: Endpoint
docs.text:
Cloud Logging has no *_EMULATOR_HOST convention. Point the client at floci-gcp by overriding the API endpoint / transport channel and disabling credentials:

  • gRPC (Java/Python/Go/Node): build the v2 client with a plaintext channel to localhost:4588 and anonymous/no credentials (see Quick Start).
  • REST: POST http://localhost:4588/v2/entries:write and :list.

docs.title: Quick Start
Filter subset
docs.text:
ListLogEntries supports a practical subset of the Cloud Logging filter language, combined with AND:

Field Operators Example logName = logName="projects/p/logs/app" severity = > >= < <= severity>=WARNING resource.type = resource.type="gce_instance" timestamp = > >= < <= timestamp>="2026-01-01T00:00:00Z" labels.<key> = labels.env="prod"

An empty filter matches all entries in the requested resourceNames. OR/NOT, functions, regex, and nested parentheses are not supported; unrecognized clauses are ignored.

docs.title: Entry semantics
docs.text:
• Request-level logName, resource, and labels are applied to entries that omit them (entry labels win over request defaults).
  • Missing insertId and timestamp are filled in; receiveTimestamp is always set to now.
  • Entries are returned ordered by timestamp (ascending by default; order_by: "timestamp desc" reverses).
  • DeleteLog removes all entries for a log name (NOT_FOUND if the log has no entries).

docs.title: Supported Operations
docs.text:
• WriteLogEntries
  • ListLogEntries
  • ListLogs
  • DeleteLog
  • CreateSink, GetSink, ListSinks, UpdateSink, DeleteSink over gRPC and REST JSON

docs.title: Sink configuration
docs.text:
Sink management accepts projects/{id}, organizations/{id}, folders/{id}, and billingAccounts/{id} parents. Each parent has its own namespace. Parent names are validated syntactically; an organization, folder, or billing account does not have to be provisioned in a separate resource catalog.

Operation REST method and path Create POST /v2/{parent}/sinks Get GET /v2/{parent}/sinks/{sinkId} List GET /v2/{parent}/sinks Update PUT or PATCH /v2/{parent}/sinks/{sinkId} Delete DELETE /v2/{parent}/sinks/{sinkId}

The LogSink.name field is the short sink identifier, such as workspace-events. Get, update, and delete requests identify the sink with the full path, such as organizations/123456789/sinks/workspace-events. List supports pageSize and pageToken. Non-positive page sizes are ignored, including when continuing from a page token.

The stored configuration includes the destination, opaque filter text, description, disabled flag, includeChildren, exclusions, and BigQuery options. Destination names can reference Cloud Storage, Pub/Sub, or BigQuery. Logging project and log-bucket destinations are unsupported. Destination existence and writer access are checked at delivery time, not when configuring a sink. Filter text is retained verbatim, including expressions outside the routing subset below.

Updates accept destination, filter, description, disabled, include_children, exclusions, and bigquery_options in the gRPC field mask, including valid nested BigQuery-option paths. REST uses the corresponding lowerCamelCase mask names, such as includeChildren. Omitting the mask uses the API's compatibility default: destination,filter,includeChildren. Fields outside the mask are preserved, and masked scalar fields can be cleared. Invalid, immutable, and output-only mask paths fail with INVALID_ARGUMENT; a failed update leaves the stored sink unchanged.

Writer identities are stable service-account principals. New unique writers are shared by sinks under the same parent, following Cloud Logging's resource-shared service-agent model. Project writers use an emulated project number; folder writers use the service-folder-{id} form observed against live GCP. Organization and billing-account allocation is deterministic emulator behavior, not a reproduction of Google's account provisioning. Existing persisted writer identities remain unchanged on reads and ordinary updates. New unique identities are computed directly from the parent. Deleting a sink does not revoke its writer's IAM grants.

Project sinks use the legacy serviceAccount:cloud-logs@system.gserviceaccount.com unless uniqueWriterIdentity=true is supplied. A legacy identity can be upgraded, but a unique project identity cannot be downgraded; updating it requires uniqueWriterIdentity=true. Non-project sinks always use a unique writer regardless of this flag. Live Cloud Logging v2 folder-sink checks on 2026-10-20 UTC confirmed creation with either flag and updates with false, true, then false retain the identity over REST and gRPC.

Writers are used directly by the internal IAM evaluator for destination writes. They do not mint OAuth tokens, inherit the ingestion caller's credentials, or call SignBlob. Sink creation does not create a user-managed IAM service account or signing key. customWriterIdentity is unsupported. Legacy project identities require Pub/Sub and BigQuery destinations in the same project as the sink. Legacy Cloud Storage delivery also requires a bucket owned by the sink's project; that check runs inside the destination policy locks at delivery time.

Sink state uses cloudlogging-sinks.json through StorageFactory and the configured global storage mode. Persistent, hybrid, and WAL storage retain configuration, writer identity, and deletion across restarts. Memory storage retains state only for the process lifetime.

docs.title: GCS export
docs.text:
After accepting a non-dry-run WriteLogEntries request, both REST and gRPC ingestion select active Cloud Storage sinks and route matching entries. Request defaults, timestamps, insert IDs, and labels are applied before routing. Enabled exclusions remove matching entries. Disabled sinks and disabled exclusions are respected. Deleting a log does not delete objects already exported. Pub/Sub and BigQuery destinations can be configured but do not receive deliveries.

Each local write produces immutable JSON-array batches of protobuf-JSON LogEntry objects, grouped by log ID and UTC timestamp hour. URL-encoded log IDs are decoded in object paths: {logId}/YYYY/MM/DD/HH:00:00_HH:59:59_S{shard}.json. Entries received in a different hour use _A{shard}:{unixTime}.json. Shards use random numeric identifiers and a create-only generation precondition, so batches never replace an existing object. Content type is application/json; internal storage fields are excluded.

This emulator delivers promptly instead of waiting for GCP's hourly batches and initial 2-3 hour latency. Failed deliveries are logged and do not fail accepted Logging writes or block other sinks. Outage buffering, automatic retries, export metrics, production shard allocation, and exactly-once delivery are not implemented. A failed batch is not replayed automatically after permissions are granted; later writes can export normally.

docs.title: Routing filters and hierarchy
docs.text:
Routing uses a strict subset independent of the lenient ListLogEntries parser:

  • AND, implicit conjunction (including newlines), OR, NOT, and parentheses. As in Logging, OR binds more tightly than AND.
  • logName, severity, resource.type, resource.labels.<key>, labels.<key>, textPayload, jsonPayload.<path>, timestamp, receiveTimestamp, insertId, trace, and spanId.
  • Equality/inequality and ordering comparisons, string containment (:), and field presence (:*). JSON numeric fields compare numerically; incompatible object/scalar comparisons and failed scalar conversions do not match. Strings use Unicode NFKC case folding for equality, ordering, and containment. Containment against numeric, Boolean, and object values does not match. Timestamp operands accept RFC 3339 timestamps or ISO 8601 dates (YYYY-MM-DD); dates use midnight UTC. Quoted label keys and JSON path components are supported, as are JSON arrays. JSON presence distinguishes explicit nulls from missing keys. Missing scalar strings use LogEntry defaults; missing map/JSON fields fail comparisons. Severity presence (severity:*) is unsupported because the ingestion model does not preserve explicit default-enum presence.

Unsupported expressions, functions, regular expressions, global searches, and unavailable payload fields stop delivery for the affected sink and produce a diagnostic. This also applies to enabled exclusions: an unsupported exclusion cannot accidentally allow the entry to escape. Configuration CRUD still retains these expressions for future support.

A sink receives logs owned by its parent. Project ID/number aliases resolve through the project registry. For folder and organization sinks, includeChildren additionally routes projects with the matching direct parent recorded by Resource Manager. Billing account relationships do not establish Logging ancestry. Nested folder ancestry is not modeled; unrelated or unknown hierarchies never match implicitly.

docs.title: Destination IAM
docs.text:
With iam.authorization-mode=enforce, grant the returned writerIdentity roles/storage.objectCreator on the destination bucket or its owning project. Export checks storage.objects.create against that principal, including supported IAM Conditions and project policy inheritance. A grant to the logging caller or source project does not grant access to a bucket owned by another project. Fresh shards need no delete permission. With enforcement disabled, export follows the emulator's usual IAM bypass.

Sink configuration, selection, and delivery share one lock. Delete, disable, filter, exclusion, and destination updates wait for any in-flight local delivery; subsequent writes see the changed configuration. Destination policy locks are held through authorization and object publication in the existing order: sink lock, IAM policy locks, bucket lock, object lock. A policy revocation is ordered before or after the publication, never between its permission check and mutation.

Sink management caller authorization remains unsupported and is tracked separately in #404.

The wire contracts follow the ConfigServiceV2 proto, the Logging v2 REST sink methods, and the Logging v2 discovery document. Export semantics follow Cloud Storage routing, shared writer identities and destination permissions, and the Logging query language. Live verification covered folder identity behavior and date-only timestamp comparisons at midnight UTC. Export file bytes and exact validation messages were not verified live.

docs.title: Managed Kafka
docs.text: floci-gcp emulates Google Cloud Managed Service for Apache Kafka (MSK) over REST JSON using the real GCP Managed Kafka API.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Variable Default Description FLOCI_GCP_SERVICES_KAFKA_ENABLED true Enable/disable Managed Kafka FLOCI_GCP_SERVICES_KAFKA_MOCK false Use mock mode (no Docker; cluster state returns ACTIVE immediately) FLOCI_GCP_SERVICES_KAFKA_CONNECT_IMAGE apache/kafka:4.3.1 Kafka Connect worker image for Connect clusters; must keep the Apache Kafka layout under /opt/kafka

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
REST API 
# Create a cluster
curl -X POST \
  "http://localhost:4588/v1/projects/floci-local/locations/us-central1/clusters" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "clusterId": "my-cluster",
    "cluster": {
      "capacityConfig": { "vcpuCount": 3, "memoryBytes": 3221225472 },
      "gcpConfig": { "accessConfig": { "networkConfigs": [{ "subnet": "projects/floci-local/regions/us-central1/subnetworks/default" }] } }
    }
  }'

# List clusters
curl "http://localhost:4588/v1/projects/floci-local/locations/us-central1/clusters"

# Create a topic
curl -X POST \
  "http://localhost:4588/v1/projects/floci-local/locations/us-central1/clusters/my-cluster/topics" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"topicId":"my-topic","topic":{"partitionCount":3,"replicationFactor":1}}'

# List topics
curl "http://localhost:4588/v1/projects/floci-local/locations/us-central1/clusters/my-cluster/topics"

docs.title: Mock Mode
docs.text: Set FLOCI_GCP_SERVICES_KAFKA_MOCK=true to use mock mode. In mock mode, clusters are created in memory and return ACTIVE state immediately without requiring a backing Redpanda container. Useful for testing Terraform or SDK code that provisions Kafka resources but does not produce or consume messages.

docs.text:
# List consumer groups
curl "http://localhost:4588/v1/projects/floci-local/locations/us-central1/clusters/my-cluster/consumerGroups"

# Get a specific consumer group
curl "http://localhost:4588/v1/projects/floci-local/locations/us-central1/clusters/my-cluster/consumerGroups/my-group"
